title: A Phenotype-Genotype Association Study Investigating Embolic Stroke of Undetermined Source
summary:
Patients who suffer a first ischemic stroke have an increased risk of having another stroke. To reduce this risk, targeted secondary preventive treatment is necessary, tailored to the underlying cause of the stroke. However, despite comprehensive diagnostics, the cause remains cryptogenic in about a quarter of all patients. To date, there is no targeted secondary preventive therapy for this group.
The PHEGAESUS study is investigating whether genetic differences can help to distinguish more accurately between patients with cryptogenic cause of stroke and those with a clearly defined etioloy. In addition, differences in certain blood parameters and their genetic regulation between the causes of stroke are also being considered as a supplementary question.
Patients with an ischemic stroke confirmed by head imaging (CT/MRI) are included. They are characterized in detail during their hospital stay using clinical information and a structured interview. A follow-up telephone interview after 90 days will supplement the data collection. Blood samples, that are not needed for routine clinical practice, will be used for genetic analysis. Stroke experts will then assign the cases to a cause of stroke. Subsequently, genetic patterns between unknown and known causes of stroke will be compared to identify possible differences. 
The PHEGAESUS study aims to unravel the mechanisms of stroke at the genetic level and thus contribute to tailored secondary preventive therapy in order to reduce the risk of further strokes in line with personalized medicine.
conditions: Stroke, not specified as haemorrhage or infarction
